utility.notes: San Pablo is a well-documented Contra Costa County city within PG&E's core Northern California service territory.

value.name: MCE (Marin Clean Energy)
value.notes: MCE's own service-area page confirms San Pablo as one of 16 Contra Costa County communities it serves (alongside Concord, Danville, El Cerrito, Hercules, Lafayette, Martinez, Moraga, Oakley, Pinole, Pittsburg, Pleasant Hill, Richmond, San Ramon, Walnut Creek, and unincorporated Contra Costa County). PG&E continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service.

permit_authority.value: City of San Pablo Building Division

permit_url.notes: The City's own dedicated Solar page, found this session (links to the Photovoltaic/Solar Panel Installation Checklist among other resources).

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own utility-wide Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes San Pablo/Contra Costa County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value.name: Drawings (3 sets; 4 sets if system is over 10kW): Site Plan, Structural Plan/Foundation Plan (if ground-mounted), Cross Sections, Structural Framing Details, Electrical Plan (18"x24" suggested minimum size)
Calculations/Specifications (2 sets): Structural Calculations (if applicable), specifications for all manufactured components (PV modules, inverter, combiner box, disconnects, mounting system)
Colored photos, inside and outside, of existing main service panels and sub-panels that are part of the photovoltaic system
Fire District Solar-Photovoltaic Notification Form (Contra Costa Fire Protection District)
Copy of fully executed contract between vendor and customer (for contractor submittals)

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own Photovoltaic/Solar Panel Installation Checklist. This is not stated to be a complete list; additional information may be required after initial plan review.

value.notes: The City's own Photovoltaic Checklist states: 'Typical plan review time for residential (one and two family dwelling) project is ten (10) working days for the first and all subsequent review cycles. Non-residential systems may take up to fifteen (15) working days for the first review cycle and ten (10) working for all subsequent review cycles.' The 10-15 range here reflects the residential (10-day) to non-residential (up to 15-day) figures; residential is the more typical case at 10 working days per cycle.

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited small residential rooftop solar (Solar Rights Act / AB 2188 compliant)
other_conditions: Electrical installations must meet Title 24 California Code of Regulations standards, including the California Electrical Code, IEEE standards, and accredited testing laboratory standards (e.g. UL)
Deviations from Title 24 requirements must be accompanied by an accredited testing laboratory approval and be approved by the building official
